title: k8s helm node provision breadcrumbs
content:
Personal scratchpad - node provisioning / helm install breadcrumbs

Context:
- Trigger: autoscaler added 3 nodes to cluster-03 during a heavy rollout (helm release: online-ingestion v2.4.0). New nodes ended up NotReady or with kubelet crashloops. Quick notes so I don't forget the sequence and commands tried.

Timeline and symptoms:
- 2026-02-28 09:12 UTC: Autoscaler created instances in ASG.
- 09:14: kubectl get nodes shows 3 new nodes in Ready=false. STATUS: NotReady, REASON: kubelet-not-ready / network-plugin failed.
- Pods on new nodes stuck in ContainerCreating or CrashLoopBackOff for kube-proxy and coredns.

Commands tried (copyable):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide
- kubectl describe node <node-name> | egrep -A3 "Conditions|Taints"
- kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/kube-proxy -l kubernetes.io/hostname=<node-name> --tail=200
- ssh ec2-user@<node-ip> -- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 | tail -n 200
- sudo systemctl status containerd.service
- sudo journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | tail -n 200
- sudo systemctl show --property=Environment kubelet
- sudo grep -R "cgroup" /etc/containerd/config.toml || true

Representative error snippets (redacted):
- kubelet: failed to register node: timed out waiting for the condition
- failed to create pod sandbox: failed to setup network for sandbox: NetworkPlugin cni failed to set up pod netns: failed to parse CNI config
- containerd: server returned error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to start containerd-shim
- cloud-init: apt/dpkg lock present, some post-install scripts timed out

What I tried and observations:
- Verified container runtime: containerd was running but restarted repeatedly on 2 nodes. journalctl showed overlayfs errors and mismatched cgroup drivers (containerd using systemd, kubelet expecting cgroupfs).
- Confirmed kubelet args differ: kubelet started with --cgroup-driver=systemd on some nodes, other nodes defaulted. Suspect AMI or cloud-init image mismatch.
- Checked helm values: network CNI version pinned in chart values is v0.9.1; nodes spun with iptables nft vs legacy iptables, CNI binary fails on nft systems.
- cloud-init logs show our userdata script tried to apt-get dist-upgrade and timed out (apt lock), leaving containerd in inconsistent state.
- I cordoned and drained one problematic node to test repro: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force. After repro, recreated node from ASG, used a different AMI (baked with prebaked containerd config) and node joined fine.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) AMI drift: recent AMI baked by infra-team changed containerd or cgroup defaults; mismatch with kubelet expectations causes bootstrap failure.
2) cloud-init race: userdata running apt operations concurrently with kubelet/containerd startup leads to partial installs and crash loops.
3) Kernel/module mismatch: overlayfs or br_netfilter not loaded on some instance types; CNI failing.
4) CNI incompatibility with nftables: nodes with nft iptables fail to apply CNI rules.

Quick remediation checklist (what fixed node in manual test):
- Select known-good AMI -> update ASG launch template to baked AMI with explicit containerd config (cgroup systemd).
- Add cloud-init quick-check loop: wait for apt locks to clear before starting kube components.
- Rebuild CNI config to handle nftables or add iptables-legacy package install in AMI.
- Add node boot-time smokecheck job that runs: systemctl is-active containerd && kubelet --version check && /opt/cni/bin/bridge --version (or simple curl to local kubelet).

Useful short commands to reproduce checks (one-liners):
- ssh and tail logs: ssh ec2-user@<ip> 'sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager'
- check cgroup driver mismatch: ssh ... 'ps aux | grep kubelet; sudo cat /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml | egrep cgroup|sudo cat /run/containerd/containerd.sock >/dev/null 2>&1 || true'
- check iptables backend: ssh ... 'update-alternatives --display iptables || sudo iptables --version'

Follow-ups / TODOs:
- [ ] Bake a new AMI with explicit containerd and iptables-legacy install + cloud-init fix (assign to infra-image). Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/815
- [ ] Add preflight user-data step to ASG launch template that waits for cloud-init to finish cleanly.
- [ ] Add ASG lifecycle hook to run smoke checks and signal success to ASG before instance moves to InService.
- [ ] Create short runbook for oncall: commands to identify cgroup mismatch and temporary workaround (reboot with proper systemd env).

Notes to self: capture AMI ids for failing nodes, collect a full journalctl --no-pager dump for one bad node and upload to artifact store. If this recurs during deploy, quickly scale down rollout and pin to previous helm chart.

Slack references: thread at slack:#infra 2026-02-28 09:20 UTC (search for timestamp)
JIRA: JIRA-INFRA-462 (investigate AMI drift)
PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/815 (image fixes)

End of scratchpad. Will update after image bake and next deploy test.
